court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, C.J. and G. Arul Murugan, J.)
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. K. Karthik Jagannath Government Advocate for R 1 and R 2
prayer: PRAYER: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the 1st and 2nd respondents herein to take action by removing the encroachment in Survey No. 296 at Orikkai Village, Kancheepuram District, by way of construction by the 3rd respondent herein, intending to place Dr Ambedkar Statue from earlier place viz. Military Road, Orikkai, Kancheepuram District.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, C.J.:— The present writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India in the nature of public interest litigation seeks a direction to Respondents 1 and 2 to restrain the third respondent from relocating the statue from Military Road, Orikkai, Kancheepuram District to Survey No. 296 at Orikkai Village, Kancheepuram District.

2. The learned counsel for Respondents 1 and 2 stated at the Bar that the proposal to re-locate the statue has been stopped. It is further stated that a Committee has been constituted in the light of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) issued on 16-9-2025 to look into the issue and take a decision. The Committee would be deciding the issue with regard to re-location of the statue. Till then, the third respondent would not be permitted to re-locate the statue on the government land.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner is satisfied with the submission made by learned counsel for Respondents 1 and 2.

4. In view of the submission made by learned counsel for Respondents 1 and 2, we dispose of the writ petition leaving it open to the Committee to take a decision in accordance with law. There shall be no order as to costs.
